reviews.title: disappointed, hidden charges and app quality has gone downhill
reviews.body:
This app has become a money grab.
I have used this app for a long time, but the current version is extremely disappointing.
The biggest issue is the subscription trap. I signed up for a trial expecting a trial experience, but I was charged afterward without a clear enough reminder. I have reported this to Apple because this kind of payment experience is not acceptable.
What makes it worse is that the app itself is getting worse every year. The workouts are outdated, repetitive, and lack creativity. It feels like the team is recycling old content instead of creating new and useful fitness programs. For a paid fitness app, the lack of fresh content is unacceptable.
I also noticed that critical reviews disappear, which makes me question how much the company values honest user feedback.
This app used to have potential, but now it feels like the priority is getting subscriptions rather than delivering a quality fitness experience.
Save your money and look for a better fitness app.

reviews.title: Toxic Fitness Culture

Plays into toxic fitness culture and manipulative marketing. When you first get started by choosing your “body type” and “goals” the imagery of the women is unreal. Cartoonish women that are busty, skinny waist, wide hips. Not how real women look. And then when you answer the motivational prompts, they ask like “do you want to get fit?” And u click yes. But then they ask you “do you want to be attractive?” This is not a motivational question to lift women up. A much better question would be “do you want to feel strong?” Or something like it. Very disappointed by this.

reviews.title: The Best Workout App in the World
reviews.body: Update, June 24, 2026 - I’ve been using this app for a while and I like it even more than when I started. It seems a person sat down and thought this through and put the exercises in the right order and the most beneficial exercises.  So, there are no surprises.  The workouts do what they say they will do.  Anyway, I do wish they’d put out some new PROGRAMS, though I’m sure at some point they will.   ———-         I am absolutely crazy about this app.  It has everything, almost (no tai chi, yet).  All types of exercises and yoga . . . Of various lengths.  I am on a 30 day dumbbell program right now.  The variety of exercises in that one program is amazing.  I’ve never seen some of those moves.  Also, doing a 7-minute workout in the morning; love those unique moves, too.  Basically, you get this and you don’t need anything else.  I downloaded dozens of workout apps and this is the one who stood out way, way above the others; nothing even compares. Totally love it!

reviews.title: Why is there such a string focus on losing weight?
reviews.body: I used to use this app for a while and it worked okay, but stopped working out and tried to redownload it. Why. Is. There. Such. A. Strong. Emphasis. On. Weight. Loss!? You can’t even log in and use the app without setting a weight loss goal! Every single exercise comes with a note on how much weight you’ll lose. I understand it’s useful if you ARE trying to lose weight, but the app SPECIFICALLY ASKS what your goals are (disappointed to find out that increasing flexibility wasn’t an option, but I guess it’s a little niche) and never once did I include weight loss. I think it’s toxic (and this is more critique of diet culture as whole rather than the app itself) to assume every goddamn person tying to stay fit is trying to lose weight. I just want to be healthy, not feel pressured into losing weight when I’m already at a healthy one. And, in the end, I don’t particularly care too much, I just deleted the app again, but what about the teenagers using this app? (There is a specific option when you log in to state you are under 18.) I don’t think it’s healthy to subject teenagers to that constant pressure, or worse, someone who has already struggled with EDs or an obsession with weight loss/appearance. It’s one thing for the option to be there, in fact, I think it’s great for those who need or want it, but the way that this is constantly shoved down your throat is ridiculous. The creators are (or at should be) fully aware that losing weight isn’t the only reason to work out, so why don’t they act like it?

reviews.title: Cannot recommend this anymore
reviews.body: 2nd attempt at reviewing this dogwater app. They’re locking previously-free features behind paywalls and ads. I’ve been using it for over a year but this is what ends my streak for good. You used to be able to change your personalized fitness routine whenever, to accommodate your needs—now it’s locked behind a subscription. There used to be a decent number of free workouts—now they’re locked behind NINETY SECONDS of ads. Every one I’ve tried so far has gotten a pop-up “watch 90 seconds of ads to get this workout free!” BRO IT WAS ALREADY FREE. IT WAS FREE BEFORE YOU STUCK FORCED ADS IN FRONT OF IT WHAT DO YOU MEAN ‘get it free with some ads’ IT WAS ALREADY FREE. And if you don’t have the “option” for ads available? YOU JUST CAN’T DO THE WORKOUT!!! And if for any reason the app resets? You guessed it: you have to watch another ad to restart the workout. Meanwhile FitOn not only has no forced ads, it also saves your progress, so if there are any technical issues, you can pick up right where you left off. I will never support an app that strips away features just to lock them behind $$$. Neither should you. Look at spotify. You used to be able to listen to whatever you wanted and skip as much as you wanted, but people kept using it after they took those things away. Turned the app into Freemium garbage. People keep using it. They keep taking features away and demanding you pay for it. STOP SUPPORTING SCUMMY PRACTICES. FitOn is free. Workout tor Women has a bunch of great free workouts. FitnessOnline even lets you make your own workout routine! Stop supporting this app until they backtrack and stop shoving ads down our throats. They WILL continue to chip away at what little free content remains until everything is plastered with ads or locked behind a subscription. Look around and see how many other companies have done the same and gotten away with minimal pushback. Stop rolling over and letting them. Previously 7/10, now absolute 0/10 will never recommend again unless they backtrack on this within the next couple of updates. I am NOT going to stop screaming about this. I am SO TIRED OF ADS INVADING LITERALLY EVERYTHING. THEY DO NOT WORK. THEY ARE A CANCER AND A PLAGUE AND MAKE EVERYTHING WORSE.
